title: Using Filter Methods to Guide Convergence for ADMM, with Applications to Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Problems
contribution: Read in its ICCOPT 2022 slides version: an augmented-Lagrangian filter wrapped around multiblock ADMM/BCD for nonconvex problems with nonlinear equality constraints, with a three-outcome convergence theorem and NMF/NMFC/spectra applications.
problem_entry: ADMM theory assumes linear constraints, fixed rho and a priori knowledge of the functions; direct multiblock ADMM can diverge for any rho (Chen et al. p=3 example); application: chemical spectrum fitting (S159 slides pp. 4-9).
key_idea: A filter on (infeasibility, first-order error of the original problem) decides when to update multipliers and when restoration plus a rho increase is needed; inner block sweeps start with a Cauchy-type projected-gradient sweep (S159 slides pp. 13-16).
assumptions: f, c in C2 (C1 for the theorem); ||c(x)|| -> inf replaced by finite bounds for compactness; block Lipschitz constants for the BCD lemma; bilinear coupling Z = XY in the applications (S159 slides pp. 3, 17, 19, 21).
proof_devices: three-outcome convergence theorem: KKT / FJ point where LICQ fails / minimizer of infeasibility, stated without proof (S159 slides pp. 17-18)
BCD sufficient-decrease lemma via a generalized Cauchy point, after Beck-Tetruashvili Lemma 3.3 (S159 slides p. 19)
experiments: NMF and NMFC (50% missing) on a 225x225 image, rho-initialization tests, comparison with Ang-Gillis accelerated NMF, 22-Gaussian spectra inversion; results only as figures not in the text layer (S159 slides pp. 21-34).
positioning: ADMM history from Douglas-Rachford to Wang et al.; Chen et al. counterexample as motivation; Vanaret-Leyffer AL filter as backbone (S159 slides pp. 6-7, 12).
writing: Talk slides by the first author (Baraldi): research framed as questions, hedged conclusion ('seems able'), a notational sign slip and typos (S159 slides pp. 7, 9, 11, 18, 35).
limits_future: Future: nonsmooth regularizers, filter convergence adjustment, accelerations, a real software package; no package at talk time (S159 slides p. 35). JOTA article not read.

method_links.note: AL filter from the home toolkit carried into ADMM, whose standard theory assumes linear constraints and fixed rho
redesign motivated by another group's smallest breaking example (p = 3 divergence for any rho)
outer filter test interleaved with inner BCD sweeps as building blocks, but a new algorithm rather than built inside an owned solver; package still future work

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: rho raised only on entry to restoration; conclusion that the filter seems able to select correct rho values; rho-trajectory tests

transferable: Update ADMM multipliers only at filter-acceptable points and raise rho only on restoration entry (S159 slides pp. 13, 16).
Filter on stationarity of the original problem, with relative stopping test omega0(xk)/omega0(x0) <= eps (S159 slides pp. 13, 15).
First BCD sweep as projected block steepest descent with step 1/L_i to obtain a sufficient-decrease bound (S159 slides pp. 16, 19).
Split bilinear NMF with Z = XY so the nonlinearity sits in a monitored constraint (S159 slides pp. 21, 26).
coauthors: Robert Baraldi (first author, presenter, Sandia), Stefan Wild

quotes.text: Monitors dual infeasibility error of the original problem while solving the augmented Lagrangian.
Filter seems able to select correct ρ values

title: Optimizing Paths for Adaptive Fly-Scan Microscopy
contribution: An iterative adaptive fly-scan framework for x-ray microscopy (gradient-based score function, uncertainty-plus-gradient acquisition objective optimized by ADAM, nearest-neighbour path, IDW completion) that reconstructs images from under 30% of raster measurements; read in the arXiv extended version.
problem_entry: Raster fly-scans waste time in uniform regions, and adaptive scanning exists only for step-scans via data-hungry deep learning; claimed first adaptive fly-scan path work (S160 arXiv pp. 2-3, 8).
key_idea: Per iteration: pick anchors by gradient score, move them by ADAM on -(alpha log U + log ||grad I||), connect them by greedy nearest neighbour instead of TSP, fly-scan, complete by IDW (S160 arXiv pp. 3-5).
assumptions: Noise-free images, sigma = 1, simulated scan physics (1 nm/pixel, 1 nm/s, 0.5 s exposure, 0.02 s dead time), raster fly-scan as reference, no motor turning limits (S160 arXiv pp. 5-8).
experiments: Four images (synthetic shapes, phantom, Cameraman, APS WSe2), 10 runs averaged, PSNR/SSIM against a same-budget random selection only (e.g. 23.7 vs 15.1 dB at 21.4%); one-at-a-time sensitivity in alpha and l on image 4; no timings, no TSP or learned baseline (S160 arXiv pp. 5-8).
positioning: Claims priority for adaptive fly-scan; placed between raster/space-filling scans, learned adaptive step-scans and matrix completion; TSP set aside on cost (S160 arXiv pp. 3, 5, 8-9).
writing: Early contribution bullets, promotional wording ('very smart'), generalization claims from four images, small numeric inconsistencies on initial sampling (7% / 6% / 7.1%), full limitations section (S160 arXiv pp. 3-9).
limits_future: Random initial path can miss localized features, sharp path angles, no noise handling; future: self-adaptive initial scan, denoising, learned or unrolled acquisition, 3D ptycho-tomography (S160 arXiv pp. 8-9).

method_links.note: problem arrives through a facility collaboration (APS data, LDRD), but no home NLP/MINLP machinery is carried in: TSP recognised then replaced by a greedy heuristic, ADAM for anchors

only a same-budget random baseline, no TSP or learned competitor, no timing or failures, hyperparameters tuned on a reported test image; first-author paper with Leyffer last, so weak evidence on his own practice
a formulation argument (exact shortest path is not the right objective) leads to a heuristic, not a better formulation

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: objective combines distance-based uncertainty and reconstruction gradient, inspired by Bayesian-optimization acquisition functions

transferable: Two-term acquisition objective: log distance-based uncertainty plus log gradient magnitude of the current reconstruction (S160 arXiv p. 4).
Gradient-proportional sampling to initialise a local optimiser over measurement locations (S160 arXiv p. 4).
Same-budget random-selection control for adaptive-sampling claims (S160 arXiv pp. 5-6).
One-at-a-time hyperparameter sensitivity with the maximum spread reported in absolute and relative terms (S160 arXiv p. 8).
coauthors: Yu Lu (first author, UC Merced and Argonne), Thomas F. Lynn, Ming Du, Zichao Di (Argonne)

quotes.text: However, solving the TSP is computationally expensive, and the true shortest path may not be optimal for our objective function, as will be discussed further in the next section.
This issue arises because the proposed framework focuses solely on path efficiency.

title: Correction: McCormick envelopes in mixed-integer PDE-constrained optimization
contribution: Corrects two mistakes in S096: adds the box constraint to the unique-solvability Assumption 2.7 2. (unbounded w can turn the PDE into an eigenvalue problem) and repairs the lim sup step of Proposition 2.14 by assuming feasibility of the projected optimum for the discretized McCormick problem.
problem_entry: Self-correction of a published convergence result: an unrealistic assumption and a proof step that used feasibility for the wrong PDE (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Repair by restricting the assumption to admissible w in [w_l, w_u] and adding an explicit compatibility/feasibility hypothesis to Proposition 2.14; only the last proof step changes (pp. 1-2).
assumptions: Assumption 2.12 parts 1 and 3 (content in S096, not read); box-restricted unique solvability; new hypothesis that (u_h, P_h w, P_h z) is feasible for (McChh) as h -> 0 (pp. 1-2).
proof_devices: Gamma-convergence-style lim inf / lim sup argument, citing Braides Prop. 1.18 (p. 2)
Lebesgue differentiation theorem for P_h z -> z, with continuity of A^-1 and j, in the recovery-sequence step (p. 2)
positioning: Cites only the original paper and Braides; no corrector credited (pp. 1-2).
writing: Counts the mistakes in sentence one, gives the mechanism of the first error, prints the corrected statements in full, states which proof steps are unchanged (pp. 1-2).
limits_future: Proposition 2.14 now conditional on a compatibility hypothesis with no sufficient condition given; impact on S096's certified example not addressed; no future work (pp. 1-2).

method_links.note: hypothesis check applied to his own theorem: assumption shown unrealistic via an eigenvalue-problem mechanism; faulty proof step located
the carried-in unique PDE solvability assumption breaks and is fixed, as SKILL.md Method 2 limitations record
step 8: claim narrowed (extra hypothesis on Proposition 2.14) rather than defended

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: repair a broken proof step by an explicit added hypothesis
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: lim sup step fixed by assuming, rather than proving, feasibility of the projected optimum for (McChh)

transferable: Erratum template: count the mistakes, give the mechanism, print corrected statements in full, say which proof steps are unchanged (pp. 1-2).
Restrict 'for all controls' well-posedness assumptions to the admissible box and check whether unbounded controls create an eigenvalue problem (p. 1).
In a recovery-sequence step, check feasibility for the discretized constraint, not the continuous one; otherwise state it as a hypothesis (p. 2).

quotes.text: We correct two mistakes in the paper [S. Leyffer and P. Manns, Math. Prog. 2025].
In the proof of Proposition 2.14, the lim sup-inequality is incorrectly derived with a feasibility argument for the PDE (2) instead of the PDE constraining (McChh).
